title: Kozarac residents protest the planned Banja Luka–Prijedor highway route
location: Magistral road Banja Luka–Prijedor, Kozarac, City of Prijedor, Republika Srpska
organizer: Kozarac residents; formal protest organizer not specified
participants_original: RTRS: around one hundred residents of Kozarac and nearby places.
threshold_50_evidence: RTRS explicitly reports around one hundred Kozarac-area residents at the February 8 protest, which supports the 50-person threshold as an approximate estimate. No exact count or range is given.

occurrence_and_demands.summary: RSE and RTRS report the February 8 protest demanding that the planned Banja Luka–Prijedor highway route be moved away from Kozarac residents’ land and properties.

location_and_organizer.summary: RTRS places residents of Kozarac and nearby places at the Kozarac-area protest on the Banja Luka–Prijedor corridor. No formal organizer is identified; a local-community chair is quoted.

participants.summary: RTRS reports around one hundred residents from Kozarac and nearby places. This is approximate; no exact minimum/maximum is derived.

dates.summary: Both reports date the gathering to February 8, 2021. Neither gives a physical end or duration.

protester_violence.summary: RSE explicitly calls the protest peaceful.

state_target.summary: The demand concerns the route of a domestic highway project; RTRS reports the plan was scheduled before the Republika Srpska National Assembly on February 9.

state_response.summary: RSE’s March 3 report explicitly identifies the February 8 Kozarac protests and quotes the RS spatial-planning minister saying the highway route would be shifted because of Kozarac residents’ complaints. This is a later accommodation announcement tied to the February demand; implementation is not verified. No event-specific arrests, beatings, dispersal, ignore, killings or shootings are reported, so those six fields remain unknown.

continuity_and_ownership.summary: RSE says residents protested several months earlier and describes subsequent route adjustment. Earlier onset and whether February 8 is a separate protest event or a later phase remain unresolved.

notes: RTRS dates the distinct local public gathering to February 8 and reports around one hundred attendees. RSE describes its peaceful nature and demand to move the planned route. RSE’s March 3 follow-up explicitly links the February protests to an official announcement that the route would shift; implementation is unverified. Earlier protests several months before February remain unresolved and are not merged.
open_questions: Review the earlier Kozarac highway-route protests and neighboring unit ownership before deciding whether February 8 is a distinct event or a phase; do not merge from campaign links alone.
Find explicit physical end/duration and any event-specific arrests, beatings, dispersal, ignore, killings or shootings.
Seek additional independent reporting and independent language review.

title: Breza residents gather outside RMU Breza in support of miners
location: In front of RMU Breza, Breza, Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
organizer: Breza residents; no organizer is named. The municipal mayor joined.
participants_original: RSE: more than one hundred residents of Breza gathered in front of RMU Breza in support of the miners’ strike; the municipal mayor joined.
threshold_50_evidence: RSE explicitly reports “more than one hundred” Breza residents gathered at the mine on February 15. The integer lower bound 101 is derived from that inequality; no upper bound or central estimate is reported.

occurrence_and_demands.summary: RSE reports that more than one hundred Breza residents gathered outside RMU Breza on February 15 in support of the miners’ strike. It describes miners’ pay, inputs and pension demands, but does not state the residents’ own demand separately; the labor-dispute category is provisional.

location_and_organizer.summary: The article places the crowd in front of RMU Breza. It says residents gathered and the municipal mayor joined; no formal organizer is identified.

participants.summary: RSE says more than one hundred residents; 101 is the derived integer lower bound. No exact number or range is given.

dates.summary: RSE dates the residents’ gathering to Monday, February 15, separate from its February 8 Zenica production stoppage and February 12 general strikes.

state_target.summary: The residents are described as supporting the miners’ strike at the mine; the article does not establish that their own demand targeted the Federation Government rather than mine management or another actor. Domestic-government target remains pending.

state_response.summary: The same article reports a government agreement ending the miners’ work stoppage, but does not link that agreement causally to this residents’ gathering. All seven response fields remain unknown for the assembly.

protester_violence.summary: No violence information is reported for the residents’ gathering; violence status remains unknown.

notes: This is a February 15 public gathering with a reported attendance above 100. It is separate from the Zenica production stoppage on February 8 and the Zenica/Breza/solidarity workplace strikes on February 12. Do not carry the miners’ agreement into this assembly’s state-response fields without an explicit link.
open_questions: Clarify whether the residents’ support directed a demand to a domestic government body or to mine management.
Find a report of the gathering’s physical end and any assembly-specific government response.
Seek independent contemporary reporting and independent language review.

title: APF union representatives gather outside Federation Government over blocked agency account
location: Outside the Federation Government headquarters, Sarajevo
organizer: Union organization of the Federation Privatization Agency (APF)
participants_original: Federalna/FENA: APF union representatives gathered; Klix and Radio Sarajevo report union representatives or a group of workers gathered. No attendance number is reported. Federalna says the agency had 25 employees; Klix says 25 families were affected. Neither figure is crowd size.
threshold_50_evidence: Attendance is not reported. APF’s 25 employees and 25 affected families are workforce/household figures, not turnout. Sources establish a group of representatives gathered, but do not establish 50 simultaneous participants.

occurrence_and_demands.summary: The opened February 15 reports describe APF union representatives or a group of workers gathering outside the Federation Government and calling for action to unblock the agency account, pay outstanding wages and contributions, and restore health insurance and basic operating resources.

location_and_organizer.summary: The gathering was outside the Federation Government headquarters in Sarajevo and was organized by APF’s union. Reports do not state that every APF employee attended.

participants.summary: Sources say “representatives” or “a group” and provide no attendee count. The reported 25 employees and 25 households are not turnout.

dates.summary: All three opened reports are dated February 15 and describe a gathering that morning.

state_target.summary: Reports explicitly say the union asked the Federation Government to unblock APF’s account and ensure unpaid wages, benefits and operating resources; domestic-government target is established.

state_response.summary: The articles report the workers’ appeal but no government action in response to this gathering, physical dispersal, arrests, beatings, killings or shootings. All seven response fields remain unknown.

protester_violence.summary: No violence information is reported; violence status remains unknown.

notes: The February 15 public gathering is separate from the APF warning strike, which Federalna reports was on its fifth day that morning. The article’s 25-employee figure and Klix’s 25-affected-families figure do not establish gathering size. FENA-origin coverage and other outlets are retained without assuming independent sourcing.
open_questions: Find any reliable attendee estimate; do not infer turnout from agency staffing or affected households.
Clarify the warning strike’s exact start and physical end separately from the February 15 gathering.
Find an event-specific government response and additional independent reporting.
